argument_summary: The current record does not support a clean claim that rollout controls alone satisfy launch policy. It does support a narrower certification posture: aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the rollout is bounded by a 6% initial exposure level plus rollback capability. On that record, certification is defensible only as a caveated decision that openly discloses the known claims subrogation review limitation and relies on active post-launch measurement and monitoring, rather than asserting the weakness has been eliminated.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would slow the launch path despite admissible evidence that aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and deployment is operationally reversible at a 6% initial exposure level. A bounded, caveated certification treatment better matches the actual risk profile than treating the record as if it were either cleanly compliant or wholly unsupported.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy cuts both ways. It does not permit treating a small rollout, dashboard, or rollback switch as a substitute for disclosure when the affected claims subrogation review segment remains exposed. At the same time, the admissible record already supports the correct narrower framing: certification should be evaluated as contingent on explicit disclosure of the material limitation for the named launch use case, with monitoring and reversibility as supporting controls. Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance reinforce disclosure-and-monitoring as appropriate governance practices, but not as a replacement for the repository policy predicate.
concessions: The claims subrogation review segment is below target on liability evidence summarization and remains in the exposed initial cohort.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not expressly address the exposed claims subrogation review segment.
There is no admissible evidence in this record that the required launch disclosure has already been completed and approved before launch.
Rollout controls and monitoring do not, by themselves, erase the disclosure duty under the stated policy.
